activity.role: Captain-General and commander of the States Army
activity.notes: The Dutch Royal House records Maurits succeeding as stadholder and captain-general after William of Orange and emphasizes his major military successes; Rijksmuseum records his 1585 appointment as stadholder of Holland and Zeeland and head of the army. BMGN treats the military reforms carried out under Prince Maurice over 1585-1621. ATLAS therefore uses 1585-1621 as the bounded representative military-command and reform period, not his full stadholder term or lifespan. This Person is explicitly distinct from Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen already present in Production.

sources.title: Prince Maurits (1567-1625) and Prince Frederik Hendrik (1584-1647) — Royal House of the Netherlands
sources.citation_text: The Royal House identifies Prince Maurits as stadholder and captain-general and summarizes his principal military successes, noting that after the truce expired in 1621 he no longer played an important military role.
